title: Darkshore
body: Darkshore is a long strip of coast on the northwestern edge of Kalimdor, a cold and misty country of grey beaches, rocky bluffs and dark evergreen woods pressed against the mountains to the east. Ten thousand years ago it was a rich land of the kaldorei empire, and Queen Azshara's Highborne dwelt in the twin towns of Ameth'Aran and Bashal'Aran, and the city of Mathystra shone in the north. The Sundering left them in ruins, and their restless dead still walk among the stones. Today the night elves hold only the port of Auberdine, and the land around it is sickening. Fel moss spreads through the woods, the Cliffspring River is turning foul, a plague has turned the thistle bears rabid, the deer are sickly, the moonkin grow hostile and the Blackwood furbolgs are openly hostile. Stormscale naga haunt the northern ruins, Greymist murlocs raid the shore, the Twilight's Hammer camps at the Master's Glaive and a warlock cult has gathered at the Tower of Althalaxx. In the remote far northeast, the Shatterspear trolls keep to themselves.

Since the gates of Ahn'Qiraj were opened, great resonating crystals of the Qiraji have broken through the earth of Darkshore, one in Twilight Vale, one by the Grove of the Ancients and one in the woods east of Auberdine. Eroded anubisath warbringers stand guard about them, and at one waits a Qiraji officer named Zod, who bids any mortal who comes near to kneel before him.

title: Auberdine
body: Auberdine is the only night elf town on the Darkshore coast, a port of low, arched timber halls among the pines, lit by lamps and guarded by Sentinels. Elder Thundris Windweaver sees to its affairs beside a village council, while Sentinels Glynda Nal'Shea and Elissa Starbreeze see to its defense. Trade has drawn others: dwarves of the Stonehammer and Steelhand families teach mining and smithing and sell their wares, and a gnome tinkers near the inn. From the northern pier the Moonspray sails for Rut'theran Village, and from the western one Elune's Blessing carries travelers to Azuremyst Isle, home of the draenei who have joined the Alliance. A moonwell and a lighthouse stand nearby.

title: Mist's Edge
body: North of Auberdine, Mist's Edge is the longest stretch of Darkshore's coast, a run of gloomy bays and grey beaches where crabs scuttle over the sand and Greymist murlocs keep their camps. The waters are worse. Threshers and coastal frenzies hunt offshore, and two ships, the Silver Dawning and the Mist Veil, lie on the seabed north of the town, sunk with their captains when murlocs fell on them as they sailed in. Their logs still rest below in lockboxes. Farther north, a shipwrecked self-styled pirate, Captain Gelkak Gyromast, curses the threshadons that sank his ship and wants his mechanical first mate, the Threshwackonator 4100, put back in working order.

title: Cliffspring River
body: The Cliffspring River runs down from the eastern mountains to empty into the sea at Mist's Edge, north of Auberdine. Its waters were once pure, but they have begun to turn foul, and Thundris Windweaver fears the wash will soon reach the town. He suspects the Blackwood furbolgs upriver, though he doubts they are the true root of it, and wants a sample drawn from the pool beneath the first waterfall, where a bridge crosses overhead. Along the banks stands the northern camp of the Blackwood furbolgs, its stores of fruit, nuts and grain heaped near a bonfire by the water, with warriors and totemics of the tribe keeping watch.

title: Cliffspring Falls
body: Cliffspring Falls spills from the mountains east and a little north of Auberdine, the source of the Cliffspring River. Behind the falling water lies a cave where rare mushrooms grow, scaber stalks and death caps that Barithras Moonshade needs for a potion. The Ancients of the Grove warned him to stay away, sensing that the cave hid a new evil in Darkshore, and their fears were well founded. Stormscale naga, wave riders and sirens, have made the cavern their lair, among them one known as Lord Sinslayer, and thugs of the Twilight's Hammer have been seen in their company.

title: Bashal'Aran
body: Bashal'Aran was one of the twin towns Queen Azshara gave to her Highborne, ruled with Ameth'Aran by Athrikus Narassin and home to his second, the mage Asterion. Both towns fell when the Well of Eternity was destroyed. Its broken stones east of Auberdine are now overrun by vile sprites, wild grells and Deth'ryll satyrs, minions of the demons who feed on the magic lingering in the ruins and grow stronger for it. There is one shrine they will not approach. On a small bluff on the western side, a strange blue aura hangs between the pillars, and within it lingers a Highborne specter.

title: Tower of Althalaxx
body: The Tower of Althalaxx rises in the north of Darkshore, northeast of Auberdine, some way removed from the twin towns it once watched over. Athrikus Narassin, Azshara's governor of Ameth'Aran and Bashal'Aran, spent most of his days here rather than among the people he ruled. Ten thousand years later the tower is occupied again. Warlocks calling themselves the Cult of the Dark Strand have gathered around and inside it, fanatics and voidcallers with a satyr, Delmanis the Hated, among them, while the most powerful keep to the upper rooms. From hiding in the nearby woods, Balthule Shadowstrike watches the cult and sends word of it to Auberdine and to his master in Ashenvale.

title: Ruins of Mathystra
body: At the northern end of Darkshore lie the Ruins of Mathystra, once a great bastion of the night elves. The city was shattered when the Well of Eternity was destroyed, and its survivors left for smaller villages along the coast to the south. Its glory has faded, but shards of its magic remain in the relics and small cat figurines scattered among the grass and broken stones. The Stormscale naga hold the ruins now, myrmidons, sorceresses and warriors guarding them fiercely, and a naga called Lady Vespira among them.

title: The Long Wash
body: The Long Wash is the shortest stretch of Darkshore's coast, running south from Auberdine, a gloomy shore strewn with debris and the carcasses of sea creatures. Great beasts of the sea have been beaching themselves here in growing numbers, and the skeleton of a sea turtle lies in the water west of the town beside a sunken ship. Greymist murlocs and crawlers pick over the sand. In the shallows lie scattered crates of elunite ore, and a restless ghost, the Shade of Elura, haunts the water around them.

title: Ameth'Aran
body: Ameth'Aran lies east of the road south of Auberdine, twin to Bashal'Aran and once a town where Azshara's Highborne practiced their powerful magic freely. When the Well of Eternity was destroyed it fell to ruin, and its people did not rest. Cursed, writhing and wailing Highborne spirits still drift among the broken walls, wielding the magical implements they used in life, and one called Lady Moongazer walks among them. Two great tablets here tell of the town and its fall. In the ruins still burns an ancient blue flame, and somewhere among the restless dead wanders the spirit of Anaya Dawnrunner.

title: Twilight Vale
body: Twilight Vale is the southern forest of Darkshore, stretching from below Ameth'Aran toward the Ashenvale border, its woods cut by the Wildbend River. Travelers do best to keep to the road. Rabid and grizzled thistle bears, moonstalkers and foreststriders roam beneath the trees, many of the deer are sick, and the Blackwood furbolgs, once friends of the night elves, prowl the vale in numbers, among them a brute called Carnivous the Breaker. Sentinel Tysha Moonblade keeps a lonely post by the road. Farther south, near the border, a Sentinel carrying word to Auberdine was ambushed and poisoned by furbolg trackers.

title: Grove of the Ancients
body: Nestled against the mountains due south of Auberdine, the Grove of the Ancients is a sacred place built among the ruins of an old night elf temple. Here dwells Onu, an Ancient of Lore, patient and wise. The night elves of Auberdine count the Ancients as venerable allies and heed their warnings. Onu has long awaited a message from the Arch Druid in Darnassus, and he is troubled that the Twilight's Hammer has come to Darkshore. Two merchants keep a small camp in the grove, and Kerlonian Evershade, a Druid of the Claw still drowsy from the Emerald Dream, has stopped here for a nap.

title: Blackwood Den
body: Blackwood Den is a cave of the Blackwood furbolgs in southern Darkshore, south of Auberdine and a short way off the road. Ursa and shamans of the tribe hold it, and they have no welcome for strangers. Volcor, master of the bear Grimclaw, has been hurt by the furbolgs and is trapped somewhere inside, unable to win his way out alone. Grimclaw has gone north to Auberdine for help, and waits by the roadside to show a rescuer the way to his master.

title: The Master's Glaive
body: In the south of Darkshore a vast blade stands driven into the earth. This is the Master's Glaive, and Onu of the Grove of the Ancients holds that it marks a place where one of the old lords of the earth, defeated long ago, fell. Now the Twilight's Hammer, a cult that worships such ancient masters, has come to it. Thugs and disciples of the cult camp at the site, crying glory and blood for the Old Gods, a firecaller named Radison among them, and in their camp lies a strange tome. A wanderer named Therylune strayed too close and found herself surrounded.

Their tome hides worse. Its script swims and twists before the eyes until it maddens, and the one page that could be torn from it proves to come from an ancient text written by elves. The cult, Onu believes, is using old elven magic to bring its masters back.

title: Remtravel's Excavation
body: In southwestern Darkshore, near the coast, the Explorers' League opened a dig under Prospector Remtravel, famed at the academy in Ironforge for his discoveries. The dwarves uncovered evidence of a great society, and then horrible golems sprang from the ground and overran the site. Cracked golems and stone behemoths still lumber among the tents. His assistant Hollee fled to Auberdine for help. Remtravel, oblivious as ever, stayed behind, chiseling at the stone and hunting for his stone brush and for a mysterious fossil he had promised to send the League.

title: Twilight Shore
body: The Twilight Shore is the long southern coast of Darkshore, running from west of Ameth'Aran down to the Ashenvale border. Greymist murlocs have built hutted camps along the sand. One of them is the haunt of Murkdeep, for whose death the Auberdine Village Council has offered a reward, and another murloc, Flagglemurk the Cruel, prowls the beaches farther north. Near the border, naga of Blackfathom and Fallenroot satyrs lurk at the water's edge, kin to those in the drowned ruins on the Ashenvale coast. The fisherman Heldan Galesong casts his line here all the same.

title: Thundris Windweaver
body: Thundris Windweaver serves as elder of Auberdine, offering sage and just stewardship of the village's daily affairs. He sees the dangers plainly: dark forces at the borders, ancient taints resurfacing and new evils rising to topple the balance of the land. He wants the Highborne implements of Ameth'Aran destroyed so the horrors of the past are not repeated, and he worries over the Cliffspring River, turning foul upstream of the town. He suspects the Blackwood furbolgs camped along it, but doubts they are the true root of the taint, and Terenthis sends him those who have scouted the furbolgs.
sources: quest 4761 description (elder, sage and just stewardship)

parts.body: The putrid river sample confirms what Thundris foresaw. He knows this corruption of old, from times past, and names Felwood as its real source. A cure might yet be tried here in Darkshore, he believes, but only with help, and he hopes to call on it when the time comes.

His friendships reach across the sea. Through his old friend Huntress Kella Nightbow, the draenei of Blood Watch send him a letter proposing an alliance. Thundris knows the isles they call Azuremyst and Bloodmyst were long ago home to his own people, recognizes some of the draenei's foes as ancient enemies of the night elves, and promises Auberdine's aid to its new allies.

title: Onu
body: Onu is an Ancient of Lore who dwells in the Grove of the Ancients, patient, wise and sparing with his words. The wind whispers to those who listen, he says, and he listens. The night elves of Auberdine count the Ancients among their venerable allies and heed their warnings, and Onu has long awaited word from Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm in Darnassus. He finds it strange that naga have come to Darkshore, and stranger still the Twilight's Hammer. He speaks to those who help him through scrying bowls and weighs what they bring in long meditation.
sources: quest 944 description (naga, Twilight's Hammer, scrying bowl)

parts.body: When the Arch Druid's message finally reaches him, Onu remarks mildly that Fandral always seems in such a hurry. The forest knows that all shall come to pass in its appointed time, he says, and Shan'do Stormrage understood that.

title: Terenthis
body: Terenthis, a druid, has come to Auberdine to learn how far the fel moss has spread through Darkshore, for the corruption of Teldrassil and the lands around it troubles the druids of the Cenarion Circle and all night elves. Some of his brethren were rescued from a corrupt furbolg on Teldrassil, and he has vowed to stop such atrocities before more of his kind are hurt or worse. He means to begin with the Blackwood furbolgs. He takes no pleasure in killing the creatures of the forest, but with no cure yet found he believes the corruption must be held back.

warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Terenthis (night elf druid in Auberdine before the Cataclysm)

parts.body: The Blackwood camp south of town confirms his fears. With corrupted furbolgs so close to Auberdine, Terenthis warns that the town must prepare itself for the inevitable, and he sends word of what was found to the elder, Thundris Windweaver.

Soon after, the bear Grimclaw comes roaring into town, moaning and stamping his paws at Terenthis. The druid calms him and casts a spell, and with it he understands the bear: Grimclaw's master Volcor is in trouble, and Terenthis promises to find someone to help him.

title: Asterion
body: Asterion was second to Athrikus Narassin when the Highborne governed the twin towns of Ameth'Aran and Bashal'Aran, a mage known for his physical prowess as much as his arcane art, who lived among the people of Bashal'Aran and saw to their needs. Now he is a specter caged by the pillars of a shrine in those ruins, held there by magic. Long centuries with only grells and satyrs for company have made his courtesy dry and barbed, and he fears his mind may never recover from them.
sources: quest 957 reward text (Athrikus his jailor, former master)
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Bashal'Aran (Narassin used a moonstone seal to imprison Asterion; still imprisoned after death)
notes: Converted: who imprisoned him (Athrikus, named only in the 957 reward text) and his release moved to part 3 on QUEST_DONE 957; the seal's trail to the satyrs to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 955, QUEST_ACCEPT 956) and its recovery to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 956, QUEST_ACCEPT 957). The opening keeps the Lay of Ameth'Aran history and his captivity (955 description). The wiki's moonstone seal by Narassin is no longer stated as fact before 957. Earlier: Verifier: verified. Faction 1: template 80, and the chain starts with Thundris (954).

parts.body: The grells' earrings carry a trace of what binds him, a seal they have touched but do not hold. Asterion guesses that it has passed to the satyrs who lead them, and the thought of being so close to passing the bars of his prison brings him near to tears.

The Ancient Moonstone Seal is taken from a Deth'ryll satyr, the work of one of the mightiest of the Highborne. For a thousand years and more it has held him, and Asterion can hardly believe he holds it now. It can be unmade in the ancient blue flame of Ameth'Aran.

With the seal destroyed, Asterion is free. He remembers a world where the Well still stood and the Highborne held court with Azshara, and he names his jailor at last: his former master, Athrikus, whom he senses still lives. Already his hopelessness is giving way to thoughts of vengeance.

title: Athrikus Narassin
body: Athrikus Narassin was a favorite of Queen Azshara, set over the twin towns of Ameth'Aran and Bashal'Aran, though he preferred the solitude of his Tower of Althalaxx to the people he ruled. Ten thousand years after the Sundering, a warlock who bears that name holds the upper room of the tower. He stands with the Cult of the Dark Strand, ringed by the strongest of its warlocks, while the cult's fanatics and voidcallers gather in and around the tower below.

Freed from the shrine of Bashal'Aran, Asterion names his jailor. It was Athrikus, his own former master, who bound him there with a moonstone seal, and Asterion senses that the old governor still lives.

Far to the south, the hunt of Delgren the Purifier finds the source of the cult master's power: soul gems in which trapped Highborne souls are held. With the last of them destroyed his power is greatly diminished, and Balthule, watching the tower, sees a blinding flash from its upper room, then screams, and lightning striking the ground.

title: Cerellean Whiteclaw
body: Cerellean Whiteclaw loved Anaya Dawnrunner of Ameth'Aran in the age when the Well of Eternity still stood. After the battles at the Well he heard that her town had been destroyed and its people killed, Anaya among them, and in his grief he followed Shan'do Stormrage into the long sleep, taking his sorrow into his dreams through the passing of the ages. Thousands of years later her memory still haunts him. Wandering the woods of Darkshore in a daze, he came upon the ruins and saw her spirit there, haunted and restless. He knows she must be freed, but he cannot raise his hand against her.
sources: quest 963 description, reward and completion text

He asks whether she hates him for what he was forced to do, begs her not to leave him, and wonders how he will face the ages of the world without her by his side.

title: Prospector Remtravel
body: Prospector Remtravel of the Explorers' League is a legend at the academy in Ironforge for his great discoveries, and a trial to anyone who works beside him. Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker assigned Hollee to work under him in Darkshore, and their dig soon turned up evidence of a great society. When golems burst from the earth and overran the site, Hollee ran for help, while Remtravel never seemed to notice. He mistakes strangers for Hollee, loses his stone brush and the fossil he promised the League, stops to admire his copy of Green Hills of Stranglethorn, and pauses mid fight to inspect a mossy stone. Hollee despairs of him.

title: Volcor and Grimclaw
body: Volcor travels the Darkshore woods with his bear Grimclaw, and can take a beast's shape himself when he needs to run. The Blackwood furbolgs wounded him in the south and cornered him in a cave, too hurt to break out alone. Grimclaw went for help, bursting into Auberdine and roaring and stamping at Terenthis until he was understood. Terenthis sewed a cloak of moonstalker pelts enchanted so that the wearer could pass Darkshore's creatures unhindered, and a rescuer wrapped in it found the bear waiting by the road. Grimclaw led the way, and at the sight of his master he rushed forward and licked his face.

parts.body: Volcor does not stay cornered. With his rescuer at his side he leaves Blackwood Den behind, either cutting a path down to the road through the furbolgs or slipping past them unseen, and word of his escape goes back to Terenthis, who takes heart that the challenges facing Darkshore can yet be overcome.

title: Wizbang Cranktoggle
body: Wizbang Cranktoggle is a gnome inventor living in Auberdine, proud of his newest creation, the buzzbox, a box with levers that lets people talk across great distances. He has set several around Darkshore, each placed near the creatures whose parts will fix its particular fault, and each, he claims, in constant need of repair. He pays anyone willing to tend them, beginning with Buzzbox 827 just south of town, which wants crawler legs.
sources: quests 983, 1001, 1002, 1003 descriptions, reward and completion texts
notes: Converted: the slurred voice moved to part 1 on QUEST_DONE 1001 and the liquor trade to part 2 on QUEST_DONE 1003; the opening is the 983 premise. quest_greeting 3666 reread: classic. parts.body: As each buzzbox hums back to life, his voice through it grows stranger. It slurs and breaks into hiccups, he insists that he is fine, and between instructions comes the sound of liquid poured into a cup, then loud gulping.

The truth comes out at the last box. The buzzboxes were never only for talking: they also brew and distill fine liquor, a trade the night elves do not appreciate in their towns. Wizbang admits the deception cheerfully and sings the praises of crawler wine, thresher ale, moonstalker moonshine and, dearest of all, thistle bear beer.

title: Murkdeep
body: Murkdeep is a murloc of the Greymist tribe who haunts a hutted camp on the shore south of Auberdine. He keeps out of sight while the camp's warriors and hunters stand. When they have fallen, fresh bands of murlocs come running at the intruder, coastrunners first and then warriors, and only with the last of them does Murkdeep himself come out of hiding to fight, hurling nets and battering at his foes.

parts.body: A notice from the Auberdine Village Council puts a price on his head. Murkdeep is held responsible for the death of at least one Sentinel and suspected of sinking at least two cargo vessels in the waters off Darkshore, and the bounty is to be claimed from Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea.
In the end Murkdeep falls on the sand among the huts he guarded, the murlocs who answered his call strewn about him, and the camp on the shore south of Auberdine is left without him.

Glynda Nal'Shea pays the bounty gladly. The citizens of Auberdine, she says, will sleep a little more soundly and safely tonight, and she names the one who slew him an executioner of justice and a true hero of the Auberdine people.

title: The Twilight's Hammer at the Master's Glaive
body: It began with mushrooms. Barithras Moonshade of Auberdine needs rare fungi, scaber stalks and death caps, for a potion, and they grow only in the cave behind Cliffspring Falls, east and a little north along the mountains. He would go himself, but the Ancients of the Grove warned him away: their venerable allies sense that the cave is the hiding place of a new evil in Darkshore. So he asks for the mushrooms to be gathered for him, and for the cave to be scouted while they are, to learn whether the Ancients' fears are true. He hopes, this time, that they are wrong.
sources: quest 961 reward text (Onu: the finding of Twilight's Hammer cultists is troubling)
notes: Converted: the opening is now the premise of 947 (Barithras); the cave's occupants moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 947), Onu's account of the Hammer to part 2 (QUEST_ACCEPT 944, also an entry trigger), the cult at the Glaive to part 3 (QUEST_DONE 944), the tome and its elven page to part 4 (QUEST_ACCEPT 951, offered on the 950 turn-in), the relics to part 5 (QUEST_DONE 951). 961 (auto-complete) not used. Earlier: Verifier: the Twilight's Hammer is named at the Glaive in 3.3.5 text (944, 949, 950, 951, 961 and creature_text 2338/2339), so title and claims kept; the furbolgs are not linked to it. 947 is the only entry point (948 requires 947, 944 requires 948); 944 kept as a second trigger. Faction 1: Barithras template 1076 and Onu template 124 are hostile to the Horde. Therylune's Escape (945) left to Ashenvale.

parts.body: The cave held what the Ancients feared: Stormscale naga, sirens and wave riders, and among them thugs of the Twilight's Hammer. Word of it reached the Grove, and Onu, patient and wise, asked at once to speak with the one who had seen them, which Barithras took as a sign of real urgency.
sources: DB: Stormscale naga, Lord Sinslayer 7017 and Twilight Thugs 2339 in the cave behind the falls

parts.body: Onu found it strange that naga had come to Darkshore, but stranger still the Twilight's Hammer, a cult that worships the old lords of the earth, defeated long ago. One such lord fell at the Master's Glaive, so he sent his visitor there with a phial of scrying, to speak with him through a bowl.

The cultists were indeed at the Glaive. The old lord impaled there is long dead, Onu said, but slivers of its power may remain, and the Hammer must be seeking them. He bade his helper search their camp for anything that might show the cult's intentions.

In their camp lay a tome hand printed in an ancient language, its script so maddening that only one page could be torn away. That page came from an ancient text written by elves: the cult was using elven magic to bring its masters back. Onu sent for relics from the Ruins of Mathystra to learn how.

The relics came from a time when Mathystra shone, a once great bastion of the elves whose glory has faded, though shards of its magic remain. Onu hopes to unlock their secrets before his enemies can, and bids his helper be vigilant.

title: The Absent Minded Prospector
body: Archaeologist Hollee had been proud to be assigned to the famous Prospector Remtravel, and the dig in southern Darkshore went well at first, turning up evidence of a great society. Then horrible golems sprang from the ground and overran the site. Hollee ran to Auberdine for help, while Remtravel, rather oblivious to his surroundings, never seemed to notice. Far away in Darnassus, Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker has had no word from his crew in weeks. Now Hollee begs anyone who will listen to travel south and see whether the prospector is still alive.
sources: Wetlands entry 1131 The Whelgar Excavation (943 onward)
notes: Converted: the opening is the premise of 729 and 730; finding Remtravel moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 729), the escort and the forgotten fossil to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 731), its delivery to Darnassus to part 3 (QUEST_DONE 741), Greywhisker's lead and Flagongut to part 4 (QUEST_DONE 942). Darkshore owns 730, 741 and 942 (Darnassus left them here); 943 stays Wetlands'. Earlier: Verifier: reframed to the Darkshore part. Greywhisker's worry (730) and his recollection of Flagongut (942) are told by darnassus.json's Greywhisker entry, and wetlands.json owns 943, so both are now only pointed at. Entry points confirmed: 730 (Greywhisker, breadcrumb for 729) and 729 (Hollee). Faction 1: 2912 and 2913 are template 55, hostile to the Horde.

parts.body: The prospector was found still at his stones, mistaking his visitor for Hollee and fretting over a lost stone brush and a mysterious fossil he had promised to send the Explorers' League. Finding it meant guarding him through the ruined camp while golems and beasts came at him from every side.

As he wandered from tent to stone, stopping to admire a book and inspect a mossy rock, Remtravel finally remembered that he had given the fossil to Hollee all along. Back in Auberdine, Hollee thanked the stars that he was safe, still unable to believe he had insisted on staying among those creatures.

Hollee would not leave Darkshore without him, so the fossil was carried across the water to Greywhisker in Darnassus. Leave it to Remtravel, the chief archaeologist exclaimed, to discover such a find.

Greywhisker had seen its like before, a fossil the archaeologist Flagongut once brought to an Explorers' League conference in Ironforge, believing it held a power that could somehow be unlocked. The trail led across the sea to Flagongut in Menethil Harbor, who could hardly believe it had come all the way from Kalimdor. What he made of it is a tale of the Wetlands.
sources: Wetlands entry 1131 The Whelgar Excavation (943 onward)

title: The Blackwood Corrupted
body: Terenthis has come to Auberdine to learn how far the fel moss has spread, and he begins his inquiry with the furbolgs. Some of his brethren were rescued from a corrupt furbolg on Teldrassil, and he has vowed to stop such atrocities before more of his kind are hurt. He has seen a few hints of corruption in Darkshore already, but no widespread signs, so he asks for one of the Blackwood camps to be found and watched for any sign of it. The Blackwood were once friends of the night elves, and if they have fallen, Auberdine stands close to danger.
sources: event_scripts 3938 (summons Xabraxxis 10373 at the northern camp)
gameobject_loot_template 14500 (Xabraxxis' Demon Bag holds the Talisman of Corruption)
warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Blackwood_tribe (corrupted by satyr interlopers led by Xabraxxis)
notes: Check: Part 1 trimmed: Terenthis's grief and the lack of a cure are 985's completion text, not shown on DONE 984 (they stay in 14818's opening); added his warning from the 984 reward. Part 2 reworded so the Felwood telling differs from 14803 and 14816 (here, the furbolgs cleared and the plan of attack from 4762's completion text). Converted: the opening is the premise of 984; the camp's corruption and Thundris moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 984), Felwood to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 4762), the satyrs' talismans and the cleansing to part 3 (QUEST_ACCEPT 4763), Xabraxxis and the talisman to part 4 (QUEST_DONE 4763). Following the coordinator's correction, the Twilight's Hammer is not linked to the furbolgs; the game text blames fel moss, Felwood and the satyrs. The Volcor branch (986-995) is told in the Volcor and Grimclaw person entry.

parts.body: The Blackwood camp south of Auberdine showed the corruption plainly. With corrupted furbolgs so close to the town, Terenthis warned that Auberdine must prepare for the inevitable, and he asked for the camp's pathfinders and windtalkers to be thinned. His findings went to Thundris Windweaver, who had ideas of his own about the cause.

Thundris doubted the Blackwood were the true root of the evil. A sample drawn from the Cliffspring River, fouling near the tribe's northern camp, pointed past the furbolgs altogether, east to Felwood, and the elder began to speak of a plan of attack.

Then came word that satyrs held the furbolgs in thrall through talismans that channel their magic. A bowl of moonwell water mixed with the tribe's own fruit, nuts and grain, set by the bonfire at the river camp, would cleanse those who ate just long enough to draw out the satyr corruptor.

The corruptor, Xabraxxis, came raging at the camp's cleansing and fell, and his Talisman of Corruption was carried back to Auberdine for disposal: one battle won in the war to reclaim the forest, and some hope that the Blackwood may one day be freed from their torment for good.

title: The Fall of Ameth'Aran
body: Sentinel Tysha Moonblade was sent to explore Ameth'Aran, east of the road south of Auberdine, where the servants of Azshara once freely practiced their powerful magics. Among the ruins she found two great tablets scrawled with the stories of the town and its fall, but the restless Highborne spirits fell on her as she read the runes, and she fled. She asks for the tablets to be deciphered in her place, so that a report can go to the Circle of Ancients. In Auberdine, Thundris Windweaver has his own concern: the spirits still wield the magical implements they used in life, and he wants those relics taken from them and destroyed.
notes: Converted: the tablets' contents moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 953, after reading them); the relics' fate to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 958). The opening is the premise of 953 and 958. 'Cataclysm' in part 2 is Thundris's own word for the Sundering (958 completion text), not the expansion. Earlier: Verifier: Tysha's flight reworded to match 953. Faction 1: Tysha and Thundris are template 80.

parts.body: Deciphered, the tablets give the Circle a rare record of the War of the Ancients. The Lay of Ameth'Aran tells how the children of the stars built their homes on the shores of the Well, where Elune was said to rest, and how Azshara set Athrikus Narassin over the twin towns, with Asterion as his second. The Fall tells of ancient trees uprooted, a sky torn by magic and brother fighting brother, and of Athrikus promising Ameth'Aran's people, with a spell, life eternal.

The Highborne relics reached Thundris, and he could almost feel the taint of their foul magic upon them. If only the tools of their undoing had been destroyed in the cataclysm that ended their world, he said; he would have them destroyed now, so that their long dormant evil is never released again.

title: The Prisoner of Bashal'Aran
body: The ruins of Bashal'Aran east of Auberdine are overrun with demonic minions, sprites, grells and satyrs that feed on the magic lingering in the stones and grow stronger for it. Yet Thundris Windweaver has noticed that there is one shrine they will not approach. On a small bluff on the western side of the ruins, a strange blue aura hangs between the pillars, and something there must explain the demons' reluctance. Thundris wants it investigated, and the one who climbs the bluff finds a Highborne specter waiting within the light.
sources: quests 954, 955, 956, 957 descriptions, reward and completion texts

parts.body: The specter was Asterion, whose dry courtesy could not hide a long and painful captivity. A seal held him there, and he asked for help finding it, for the earrings worn by the grells might carry a trace of it.

The earrings showed the seal had passed through the grells' hands to the satyrs who led them, and from a Deth'ryll satyr came the Ancient Moonstone Seal itself, the work of one of the mightiest of the Highborne. It could be destroyed in the ancient blue flame that still burns in Ameth'Aran, twin of his town.
sources: creature_loot_template: Ancient Moonstone Seal 5338 from Deth'ryll Satyr 2212; Grell Earring 5336 from Wild Grell 2190 and Vile Sprite 2189

parts.body: When the seal was destroyed, Asterion was free for the first time since the Well of Eternity stood. He named his jailor, his former master Athrikus, sensed that he still lived, and felt his despair give way to thoughts of vengeance.

title: The Tower of Althalaxx
body: Sentinel Elissa Starbreeze is charged with keeping Auberdine from harm, and to that end she sent Balthule Shadowstrike to watch the strange happenings at the Tower of Althalaxx, northeast of the town. He should have returned long ago. Elissa fears that he has met some unforeseen danger in the forest, and she asks for someone to find him and see that he is well. The tower once belonged to Athrikus Narassin, Azshara's governor of the twin towns, and of late it has drawn unwelcome company.

Ashenvale owns 970, 973, 1140 and Delgren the Purifier (3663); the soul gem hunt is no longer told here. Only 965 is a trigger. Faction 1: Elissa and Balthule are template 80.

parts.body: Balthule was found alive, still at his post near the tower, with troubling news he had no means to deliver. Warlocks had gathered around and inside the tower, and he had stayed for fear of missing something. His master Delgren had suspected such a gathering but not its purpose, and the scraps of parchment the warlocks carry might complete the puzzle.

The parchments gave the company a name, the Cult of the Dark Strand, though Balthule knew nothing of its history or plans. His master, Delgren the Purifier, is a paladin who helps the Sentinels against demons and undead, and Delgren must know of the cult at once, so Balthule's letter was bound south for him at Maestra's Post in Ashenvale.

The hunt for the cult's power was carried through in Ashenvale, and when it was done, Balthule had news of his own: a blinding flash from the upper room of the tower, then screams, and lightning striking the ground. The time had come to strike, for Athrikus, master of the cult, kept to the top of the tower among warlocks far deadlier than those below.

Athrikus Narassin fell at the top of his tower. Balthule hoped the demonic forces would be driven back, though he had no doubt they would regroup and return, and he bade that word be carried south to Delgren: Athrikus lay stilled, and the Cult of the Dark Strand was beaten and scattered.

title: Tharnariun's Hope
body: A sickness spreads across Darkshore, gripping the minds and bodies of all it touches, and the thistle bears have suffered worst, once noble beasts made rabid and frenzied. Tharnariun Treetender of Auberdine hopes he has a cure. He has made a trap of light to be laid in the forest: any rabid bear that crosses it should grow docile for a short time and follow whoever set it. He asks for one to be led back to him alive, and if a trap is lost he will make another, for Tharnariun's hope, he says, is eternal.
sources: quests 2118, 2138, 2139 descriptions, reward and completion texts
notes: Converted: the opening is the premise of 2118; the failed cure moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 2118, QUEST_ACCEPT 2138), the Den Mother to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 2138, QUEST_ACCEPT 2139), his thanks to part 3 (QUEST_DONE 2139). npc_text 769 reread: a plain greeting. Earlier: Verifier: 'a hunter' changed to 'his helper' (could read as a class). Faction 1: Tharnariun is template 80.

parts.body: The cure failed. With sorrow Tharnariun ordered the sick and tainted bears put down, knowing it would not stop the plague, only slow the damage the animals were doing to the forest and its people for a short time.

Even that was not enough. The rabid bears were still spreading into the land from a cave to the northeast, near Bashal'Aran, where the infected Den Mother dwelt, and Tharnariun asked for one last killing, hoping it would be the last time he had to call on his helper.

With the Den Mother slain, fewer rabid bears entered the land. Tharnariun gave thanks, for in these war torn lands, he said, many will not rise to the challenge of life in their new home, and choose to hide in their homes or flee to the more fortified lands of the Alliance.

title: Washed Ashore
body: Great creatures of the sea have long been known to fling themselves onto the Darkshore coast and die there, but lately they have been washing ashore in ever greater numbers. The Temple of the Moon has sent Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde to Auberdine to learn why, to help the troubled people of the town. Greymist murlocs make her work hard, ringing a giant carcass on the beach just south of the town, so she asks for help gathering its bones for study in Darnassus. She cannot help thinking the strandings are an ill omen.
sources: quest 3524 description, reward and completion text
notes: Converted: the opening is the premise of 3524 (with her gossip, npc_text 5943); the bones and the second find moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 3524, QUEST_ACCEPT 4681), the Teldrassil idea to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 4681). npc_text 5943 reread: classic. Earlier: Verifier: verified. Faction 1: Gwennyth is template 80. The follow-up beached creature quests (4722-4733) are Alliance only and not used as triggers.

parts.body: The bones went north on the next hippogryph to Darnassus. The stranding was no isolated case, Gwennyth found: more creatures lay along the coastline and in the water, and she sent her helper on to the remains of a sea turtle west of Auberdine, near a sunken vessel.

The turtle's remains gave her a real chance at the mystery, and the idea that troubles her most is that the creatures may be fleeing the waters around Teldrassil. Her research, she says, is but in its infancy, and she asks to hear of any other beached creatures found along the coast.

title: The Red Crystal
body: The moonkin of Darkshore were once thought gentle, almost mystical creatures, and some still revere them, but Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea must keep Auberdine safe, and hostile moonkin now roam east of the town in growing numbers. Reports claim they are being drawn to a large red crystal along the eastern mountains, though no one knows what it is, or whether it even exists. Glynda wants it found and reported on, so that the town can learn why the moonkin gather there and whether the thing is benign or holds some more sinister purpose.

parts.body: The crystal exists, and Glynda means to examine it closely. She suspects it is tied to Felwood, which lies above Darkshore to the east, and has moonwell water carried to it to be poured over its surface, since such potent magic should reveal something of what it is made of.

Up close the crystal looks alien against the wooded hills, and a faint humming seems to come from deep within it. As the water cascades down its lattices, the opaque surface turns clear, revealing small fragments of bone and half a jawbone, seemingly a humanoid's, locked inside a stone that even the strongest magic could hardly break.
sources: quest 4812 completion and reward text (at the crystal, gameobject 175524)

parts.body: The answers raised only more questions. Glynda took them to the town council, hoping it would know what course to follow, if any, and she remains content for now that the threat lies far enough to the east to be out of harm's way.
